Operator: Good morning, and welcome to the Apex Energy Corp. Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants will be in listen-only mode. After today's presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. [Operator Instructions] Please note this event is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the conference over to John Smith, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

John Smith: Thank you, Operator, and good morning, everyone. Welcome to Apex Energy Corp.'s Q3 2024 earnings call. Joining me on the call today are David Thompson, Chief Executive Officer; Lisa Chen, Chief Financial Officer; Mike Rodriguez, Chief Operating Officer; Sarah Jenkins, VP of Exploration; and Tom Rivera, VP of Marketing.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that some of the statements we make today may be forward-looking. These statements are based on current expectations and assumptions and are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a more detailed discussion of these risks.

I will now turn the call over to David Thompson.

David Thompson: Thank you, John, and good morning, everyone. Apex Energy Corp. delivered solid results in Q3 2024, driven by strong operational performance and favorable commodity prices. We achieved strong environmental performance with reduced spills and proactive remediation. I'm particularly pleased with our progress on exploration and drilling activities, highlighted by exceptional well results. We are focused on midstream segment growth through higher transportation volumes and infrastructure expansions. Further, we are working on capital expenditure efficiencies across drilling, completion, and facilities. We continue to adjust to production guidance shaped by operational tailwinds. Finally, we are taking steps to optimize capital allocation priorities including dividends, buybacks, and targeted reinvestments.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Lisa Chen to discuss our financial results in more detail.

Lisa Chen: Thank you, David. As David mentioned, we had a strong quarter. Our revenue was $2.8 billion, up 22% year-over-year. Operating income was $950 million, and net income was $720 million. We generated $850 million in free cash flow and returned $500 million to shareholders through dividends and share repurchases. Our balance sheet remains strong, with $4 billion in debt and $2 billion in cash.

Thank you, David, and good morning, everyone. As we continue to deliver strong operational and financial results in Q3, I'd like to spend a few minutes on our environmental performance, specifically around spills, incidents, and remediation efforts. Safety and environmental stewardship remain core to our value proposition at Apex Energy Corp., underpinning our license to operate across our diversified portfolio in the Permian Basin, Gulf of Mexico, and emerging plays in Guyana. We're proud to report continued progress toward our 2025 goal of zero reportable spills greater than 1 barrel, aligned with API Recommended Practice 75 and our internal Leading Environmental Indicator framework.

Let's start with the numbers. In Q3 2024, we experienced two reportable spills totaling 18 barrels—a 60% volume reduction quarter-over-quarter and a remarkable 73% year-over-year decline from the 67 barrels across five incidents in Q3 2023. For the full nine months, we've had just five reportable spills aggregating 120 barrels, down from 12 spills and 450 barrels in the same period last year. This puts our spill rate at 0.12 barrels per million production hours, well below the industry average of 0.45 reported by the American Petroleum Institute's aggregated data for upstream operators, and competitive with peers like ExxonMobil's 0.18 rate in their latest sustainability report.

Breaking it down by region: In the Permian Basin, which accounts for 65% of our upstream production, we had one minor onshore spill of 8 barrels from a third-party midstream connector failure—quickly contained using our rapid-response absorbents and vacuum trucks, with no impact to waterways. This reflects a 85% drop in Permian spill volumes YoY, driven by our full-field rollout of SCADA-integrated leak detection systems. Offshore in the Gulf of Mexico, our deepwater assets saw zero spills this quarter, maintaining a flawless record for the year-to-date—a testament to post-Macondo enhancements like subsea integrity monitoring with ROVs and acoustic sensors. Internationally, in our Guyana Stabroek block joint venture with ExxonMobil and Hess, we reported one 10-barrel bunker fuel release from a supply vessel, fully mitigated within 24 hours using dispersants compliant with Guyana's EPA protocols—no wildlife or habitat impacts.

On incidents more broadly, our Total Recordable Incident Rate (TRIR) for environmental events stood at 0.08 per 200,000 man-hours in Q3, a 20% improvement from Q2 and 33% better than 2023. Lost Time Incident Rate (LTIR) for spill-related events is now at 0.03, reflecting proactive measures like our AI-driven predictive analytics platform, which flagged 47 potential leaks before they escalated, preventing an estimated 250 barrels of potential releases.

Turning to remediation efforts, we've closed out 95% of active legacy sites from pre-2020 incidents, with total spend of $15.2 million YTD—flat YoY despite inflationary pressures on labor and materials. Key highlights include the full bioremediation of a 2019 45-barrel crude release in the Delaware Basin, where indigenous hydrocarbon-degrading microbes reduced TPH (total petroleum hydrocarbons) levels from 5,200 ppm to below 50 ppm Maine DEP risk-based standards in just 14 months, at a cost of $2.1 million. In the Gulf, we're advancing in-situ chemical oxidation at two historical platform sites using persulfate injections, achieving 92% groundwater plume reduction per third-party audits. We've also deployed over 1,200 miles of optical fiber DTS (Distributed Temperature Sensing) across pipelines for real-time anomaly detection, slashing remediation timelines by 40% on average.

Strategically, these outcomes stem from our $250 million three-year investment in NextGen Environmental Tech, including partnerships with SLB for drone-based LiDAR hyperspectral imaging—now covering 80% of our Permian acreage—and Baker Hughes' Cordant™ digital well integrity software, which has boosted our pipeline ILI (In-Line Inspection) efficiency by 25%. We're on track for SPCC (Spill Prevention, Control, and Countermeasure) Plan recertification across all BSEE-regulated assets, and our ESG scoring has climbed to an MSCI AA rating, up from A last year.

Looking ahead, with WTI at $82 and Brent holding firm amid OPEC+ cuts, we're allocating an incremental $50 million from free cash flow to accelerate toward net-zero Scope 1/2 emissions by 2035, including flaring reduction to under 1% in the Permian via our electrified drilling rigs with GE Vernova. Minor incidents like those this quarter underscore the industry's inherent risks, but our trendline—five straight quarters of spill volume under 50 barrels—positions us as a leader in responsible operations. Regulatory tailwinds from the EPA's updated methane rules further incentivize our low-impact profile, supporting margin resilience.

Before we move on, let me walk you through our capital expenditure breakdown for the quarter and year-to-date, focusing on our core Drilling, Completion, and Facilities categories. As you know, Apex's 2024 capex program is anchored at $1.6 billion, with a disciplined allocation of 52% to Drilling, 38% to Completion, and 10% to Facilities. This reflects our returns-focused strategy in the Permian Basin—where we hold over 300,000 net acres of Tier 1 inventory—and selective investments in the Eagle Ford and Gulf of Mexico shelf.

Year-to-date through Q3, we've deployed $1.2 billion in total capex, tracking slightly ahead of our budget due to accelerated efficiencies. Drilling capex came in at budget $410 million YTD versus actual $385 million, a 6% underrun, as we spudded more wells than planned with superior metrics. Completions were budget $295 million versus actual $305 million, a slight overrun from proppant dynamics but offset by cycle time gains. Facilities saw budget $65 million versus $95 million actual, driven by Permian debottlenecking investments that enhance utilization.

These variances highlight our manufacturing-style execution, with Permian drilling efficiencies at 1.85 days per 1,000 feet and completions yielding half-cycle returns over 100%. Full-year capex remains $1.58-1.62 billion, supporting robust free cash flow.

Thank you again, David. Moving now to our production guidance for next quarter and the full year, I'm pleased to reaffirm our disciplined approach to capital allocation amid a constructive macro environment. With WTI holding steady around $80 per barrel and Brent at $85, supported by ongoing OPEC+ production cuts and resilient global demand—particularly from LNG exports to Europe and Asia—we're positioned to deliver organic growth while protecting our balance sheet.

For Q4 2024, we guide to 270,000 to 280,000 barrels of oil equivalent per day (boepd), representing a 4-7% sequential increase from Q3's realized volumes. This uplift is driven primarily by our Permian Basin assets, where we'll bring online 25-30 new D&C wells in the Delaware sub-basin, leveraging extended laterals and proprietary frac designs.

On the full-year 2024 guidance, we maintain our range of 265,000 to 275,000 boepd, implying full-year growth of 8-12% over 2023. Key factors include operational efficiencies like 18-day drilling cycles, regional dynamics with Permian leading growth, and mitigants for headwinds such as turnarounds. Base declines are offset by new well additions, with hedges derisking the profile.

Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining our Q3 2024 earnings call for Apex Energy Corporation. As we wrap up another strong quarter with adjusted EBITDA up significantly, it's the perfect time to dive into our capital allocation framework. Our priorities remain laser-focused on delivering superior total shareholder returns while positioning Apex for long-term value creation. We generate industry-leading free cash flow, projected at $8.5 billion for full-year 2024, thanks to low-cost Permian inventory and unit LOE at $4.50 per BOE.

Our philosophy: first, sustainable dividends; second, opportunistic share buybacks; third, high-return reinvestments. In Q3, we declared $0.45 per share dividends, up 10%, and repurchased shares under our $3 billion program. Capex at $11.2 billion yields 5% growth, focused on upstream, midstream, and tech. We've returned 55% of FCF to shareholders YTD, balancing growth and returns.

I will now turn the call over to Mike Rodriguez for an operational update.

Mike Rodriguez: Thank you, Lisa. On the operational front, we continue to execute our strategy effectively. Our production averaged 265,000 barrels of oil equivalent per day. We successfully brought Apex 12H-4 online, which is expected to contribute significantly to our production growth in the coming quarters. We are also making progress on our cost reduction initiatives, including water recycling and electrification.

Now I will turn it over to Sarah Jenkins for an update on our exploration activities.

Sarah Jenkins: Thank you, Mike. Good morning, everyone. This is Sarah Jenkins, our Executive Vice President of Exploration and Production. I'm pleased to provide an update on our drilling and exploration activities during the quarter, which continue to demonstrate the strength of our high-quality inventory and operational efficiencies. With WTI crude averaging $82 per barrel and Henry Hub natural gas at around $2.80 per MMBtu, we've maintained a disciplined approach, focusing on our oil-weighted assets in the core of the Permian Basin while advancing key tests in the Eagle Ford and Gulf of Mexico shelf.

We spudded 28 wells across our portfolio, brought online 32 gross operated wells, and achieved an average drill time of 18 days from spud to rig release—down 12% sequentially and 25% year-over-year, thanks to our optimized pad drilling program using high-spec rigs equipped with our proprietary automated drilling systems. Completion costs per lateral foot fell to $650, a 15% reduction from Q2, driven by higher proppant intensity—now averaging 2,500 pounds per foot—and the rollout of our next-gen dissolvable diverter technology, which improved cluster efficiency to 92%.

Our standout performer this quarter was the Apex 12H-4 well in the Delaware Basin portion of the Permian, our first 20,000-foot lateral in the Second Bone Spring bench. It posted an IP30 of 4,250 boe/d, with 78% oil cut—beating our basin type curve by 28%. In the Midland Basin, our five-well Northern Midland pad averaged IP30s of 2,800 boe/d. Eagle Ford laterals posted 1,950 boe/d, and Guyana's Yellowtail-2 appraisal flowed 8,500 bbl/d. No dry holes; success rate at 98%.

Efficiency metrics remain world-class: rig productivity at 2.1 wells per rig-month, flat time reduced by 30%. Sustainability efforts include 100% grid power on three pads and 85% water recycling.

Looking ahead, we're guiding for 120-130 gross operated wells in 2025, with capex allocation emphasizing longer laterals and pilot tests. We're accelerating Gulf deepwater exploration and progressing farm-downs. Amid OPEC+ support, we're prioritizing capital velocity, growing production 8-10%. These results underscore our tier-1 inventory durability.

Finally, I'll turn it over to Tom Rivera to discuss our marketing strategy.

Tom Rivera: Thank you, Sarah. Thank you, Operator, and good morning, everyone. I'll now turn to our Midstream segment performance, where we continue to deliver strong, fee-based cash flows amid robust upstream production growth and expanding export markets. For the quarter, Midstream generated adjusted EBITDA of $285 million, up 18% year-over-year and 5% sequentially, driven by higher transportation volumes across our crude, natural gas, and NGL systems, as well as contributions from recently placed infrastructure assets.

We achieved record throughput of 2.8 million barrels of oil equivalent per day across our network—a 14% increase from Q3 last year. Crude oil volumes at 1.45 million barrels per day, up 16% YoY, from Permian systems running at 92% utilization. Natural gas at 4.1 Bcf/d, NGL fractionation at 285,000 bpd. Permian accounts for 55%, with growth in Bakken and Gulf exports.

We deployed $420 million in midstream capex this quarter, including Permian Highway Pipeline expansion adding 250,000 bpd. Advancing CO2 sequestration hub and Nederland Terminal expansion. Prioritizing dropdowns for fee-for-service model, 92% of EBITDA fixed-fee.

Q4 volumes at 2.9 MBOE/d, EBITDA $290-300 million; full-year $1.15 billion. Our diversified footprint positions us well.

Operator, we are now ready to open the line for questions.

Operator: [Operator Instructions] Our first question comes from Joe Harris with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

Joe Harris: Good morning. Can you provide more detail on the spills and remediation efforts this quarter?

Lisa Chen: Good morning, Joe. As I detailed earlier, we had two reportable spills totaling 18 barrels, a sharp decline YoY, with quick containment and no environmental impacts. Our remediation closed 95% of legacy sites, backed by tech investments like DTS fiber and AI analytics. This keeps us below industry averages and on track for our 2025 zero-spill goal.

Operator: Our next question comes from Emily Chen with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Emily Chen: Good morning. What are your expectations for production guidance factors into 2025?

Lisa Chen: Good morning, Emily. Our full-year 2024 guide holds at 265-275k boepd, with Q4 at 270-280k. Into 2025, tailwinds from Permian D&C, Eagle Ford lifts, and Gulf tie-backs drive 8-12% growth. Headwinds like turnarounds are mitigated by hedges and 95% success rates.

Operator: Our next question comes from Mark Lopez with Barclays. Please go ahead.

Mark Lopez: Could you please provide more color on capex breakdown variances?

Lisa Chen: Thanks, Mark. Drilling underrun from efficiencies saved $25 million YTD, completions slight overrun offset by contracts, facilities advanced for debottlenecking. Overall, 98% budget efficiency supports FCF generation.

Operator: Our next question comes from Rachel Kim with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Rachel Kim: How will the results of the exploration program affect the company's future strategy?

Sarah Jenkins: Good morning, Rachel. The Apex 12H-4 and pad results validate our inventory, with 4,500 locations at >60% IRR. This shifts focus to longer laterals and Permian bolt-ons, freeing capital for high-return Gulf wildcats while growing output 8-10%.

Operator: Our next question comes from David Patel with Citigroup. Please go ahead.

David Patel: What is the outlook for the midstream segment in the coming years?

Tom Rivera: Good morning, David. Q4 EBITDA $290-300M, full-year $1.15B. Long-term, expansions like Permian Highway and CO2 hubs yield mid-teens IRRs, with 92% fixed fees insulating volatility and export growth driving volumes.

Operator: There are no further questions at this time. I would like to turn the conference back over to David Thompson for closing remarks.

David Thompson: Thank you, Operator. In summary, we are pleased with our performance in Q3 2024. We remain focused on executing our strategy and delivering value to our shareholders. Thank you for joining us today.

Operator: This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
